title: Record speed with every answer
statement: Record how long each answer took as well as whether it was right, since a fast wrong answer marks a confident misconception and a slow right one fragile knowledge.
detail: A practice BrainLift in the reading course's feedback sorts answers into four cells: fast and correct is fluent, slow and correct is fragile and calls for a shorter interval, fast and incorrect is a confident misconception that needs discrimination practice, and slow and incorrect is not yet acquired; platforms that rely on accuracy alone will systematically misclassify learners. The course's instruction standard adopted the four-cell diagnostic to drive scheduling (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/instruction-quality-standard.md`, line 125).

evidence.quote: slow correct (fragile, shorten interval), fast incorrect (confident misconception, needs discrimination practice)
Platforms that rely on accuracy alone will systematically misclassify learners
The four-cell diagnostic (fast/slow × correct/incorrect) drives scheduling.
